column1: # rawjournal-archive-unfilable-dates.tsv — the ONE fixture family in this corpus whose
# column 2 is LITERAL, not an offset from now.
# WHY IT IS ALLOWED TO BREAK THE OFFSET RULE. The rule exists because staleness is
# defined relative to now, so a frozen timestamp decays from live to stale and the
# fixture stops meaning what it says. Every row here is a value that is NOT A
# TIMESTAMP AT ALL — that is the entire subject of the file. There is nothing for an
# offset to express, and materialising these through `date -u -d @<epoch>` would
# destroy the only property under test. `rawjournal-*.tsv` is copied byte-for-byte
# (comment and blank lines stripped); `journal-*.tsv` is materialised from offsets.
# Nothing that depends on now may be written here.
# WHAT IT MEASURES. do_archive builds a filename from characters 1-10 of field 2. The
# only thing standing between that and an arbitrary write path is one shell `case`
# glob. Rows 1 and 2 are chosen so that removing that guard writes OUTSIDE the archive
# directory into a directory that EXISTS — repo root and docs/loop/ — because a
# traversal that lands in a directory nobody created fails on the redirect and would
# let the probe pass for the wrong reason:
#   ../../../x  -> <root>/x.tsv                     (escapes the whole docs tree)
#   ../KPI.md   -> <root>/docs/loop/KPI.md.tsv      (lands beside the registers)
# The remaining rows are the ordinary garbage a hand-appended journal produces.
# The last row is NOT an escape and IS archived: 9999-99-99 satisfies the glob, which
# tests SHAPE and not the calendar. That is a stated limit of the guard, asserted here
# so it stays measured rather than described.
